notes: A condition-name's literal is associated with its conditional variable's description; a group has no PICTURE, let alone a signed numeric one, so a signed numeric literal on its level 88 entry violates SR2. '01 G. 88 G-N VALUE -1. 05 A PIC X(2).' compiles at --std 85 and G-N tests the characters '-1' (prints G-N TRUE). Every elementary case of the read is refused as required; only a group conditional variable escapes. kb/Work PB5215 holds the defect (code read: held-85/set2/decisions.json).

next.reason: 1985 requires 'a signed numeric PICTURE character-string' for a signed numeric literal, and §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b gives numeric edited items nonnumeric literals only. §2023:13.18.63.3 SR3 admits 'either a signed numeric data item or a numeric-edited data item with a representation of a sign', and §2023:13.18.63.3 SR6 lets numeric literals initialize numeric-edited items 'such that no truncation of digits or sign is required'. A signed literal for a numeric-edited item, refused in 1985, is accepted. SR3 is an all-formats rule, so it also governs condition-name values. Both editions refuse at compile time.
